novel_features.name: Concept chronology
novel_features.description: See how Seykota's thinking on a concept appears across 20 years — a year-ordered list of every FAQ month, TSP section, and risk-essay passage that matches your query.
novel_features.rationale: Requires bucketing the local FTS5 index over the entire crawled corpus by year and merging FAQ, TSP, and risk hits into one timeline — the site's Google search box is undated and unordered.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when you need the evolution of a trend-following idea over time, not just its latest mention.

novel_features.name: Coin-Toss simulator
novel_features.description: Monte-Carlo the risk essay's own Coin-Toss / fixed-fraction model with your win rate, payoff, and bet fraction — reports median terminal equity, probability of ruin, max drawdown, and the optimal-f comparison.
novel_features.rationale: The essay walks through this simulation in prose but nothing on the site runs it; the CLI turns a named model unique to this corpus into a seeded, deterministic command.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to stress-test a position-sizing fraction against ruin before you trade it.

novel_features.name: Lake Ratio calculator
novel_features.description: Compute Seykota's Lake Ratio — the area of drawdown 'water' divided by the area under the equity 'land' — over your own equity curve from a CSV or stdin.
novel_features.rationale: The essay defines the Lake Ratio only qualitatively via the lake metaphor; reducing a real equity series to the number exists nowhere as a tool.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to score how 'underwater' a strategy's equity curve spends its time, beyond max drawdown.

novel_features.name: FAQ contributor index
novel_features.description: List everyone who wrote into Ed's FAQ with how many months each appears in, or pass a name to see exactly which months they show up in.
novel_features.rationale: seykota.com has no contributor index; this aggregates parsed contributor lines across all ~266 month-pages held in local SQLite, exploiting the FAQ's reader-mailbag structure.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when cross-referencing or citing recurring FAQ contributors in research notes.

novel_features.name: Metric explainer
novel_features.description: For a named risk metric — heat, Kelly K, the Uncle Point, the Lake Ratio, the Timid/Bold trader rules — print the exact passage from the risk essay that defines it plus the calculator subcommand that runs it.
novel_features.rationale: The site keeps the prose essay and any calculation entirely separate; this maps a curated metric vocabulary onto the defining essay section and the matching `risk` subcommand.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to get the definition and the formula together before you compute anything.

novel_features.name: Citation-formatted search
novel_features.description: Search the archive and get back one ready-to-paste citation per hit — source, date or section, snippet, and URL — or BibTeX entries.
novel_features.rationale: Turns FTS5 hits into attributed quotes using the per-row date/section/URL metadata the raw site never surfaces alongside the text.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this whenever you need to quote Seykota with a real citation in a write-up or a tooltip.

narrative.headline: Ed Seykota's Trading Tribe archive on the command line — 20 years of FAQ, the Trading System Project rules, and the risk-of-ruin essay, searchable offline, with the position-sizing calculators built in.
narrative.value_prop: seykota.com is the canonical primary source for trend-following risk control, but it's a sprawling 1990s static site with no search worth using and no calculators. This CLI ships a vendored snapshot of the FAQ months, the TSP sections, and the risk essay so `search`, `faq`, `tsp`, and `risk show` work with zero network — and it turns the essay's math into runnable commands: `risk kelly`, `risk heat`, `risk uncle-point`, `risk coin-toss`, `risk lake-ratio`. `timeline` shows how a concept appears across 20 years; `cite` gives you attributed quotes; `risk explain` ties each metric to the passage that defines it.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the offline index works — top FAQ/TSP/risk hits on portfolio heat with source URLs.
The essay's Kelly fraction, K = W - (1-W)/R = 0.25, as a one-liner.
Per-trade risk and share count for one position; add --positions to sum portfolio heat.
The Trading System Project's exponential-crossover system rules.
Every place Seykota addressed whipsaws, in chronological order.
Re-crawl seykota.com to refresh the local index; add --full-archive for the pre-2010 day-pages.

troubleshoots.fix: The vendored snapshot ships with the binary; run `seykota doctor` to confirm the DB path, or `seykota index build` to (re)build it from the live site.

troubleshoots.symptom: index build is slow or gets throttled
troubleshoots.fix: The crawler is rate-limited on purpose (~1 request/second) — a full refresh of ~270 pages takes a few minutes; let it finish.

troubleshoots.symptom: a FAQ search hit lands on a month page, not the exact exchange
troubleshoots.fix: The MVP index stores one row per month-page; use `faq show <year> <month>` and search within, or grep the page text — per-exchange indexing is intentionally deferred.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent or operator needs Ed Seykota's actual words on trend following, position sizing, heat, pyramiding, exits, or trading psychology — with a citeable source — or needs to run the position-sizing math from his risk essay (Kelly, heat, Uncle Point, Coin-Toss simulation, Lake Ratio) on concrete numbers. It is the right choice over a generic web search because it is offline, structured, dated, and the calculators match Seykota's exact formulations.

recipes.title: Quote Seykota on a topic with a citation
recipes.explanation: Returns FAQ hits formatted as citations — month, snippet, URL — ready to paste into a research note or a tab tooltip.

recipes.title: Size a position the way the essay prescribes
recipes.explanation: Per-trade dollars at risk, share count, and the resulting heat percentage as compact JSON for piping.

recipes.title: Stress-test a betting fraction against ruin
recipes.explanation: Monte-Carlos the essay's Coin-Toss model and reports ruin probability, median terminal equity, and max drawdown deterministically.

recipes.title: Trace a concept across the archive
recipes.explanation: A year-ordered list of every FAQ month, TSP section, and risk passage that mentions trend following — narrowed to the fields an agent needs.

recipes.title: Read the TSP system rules offline
recipes.explanation: Prints the support-and-resistance system section of the Trading System Project, with its last-updated date and links, from the local snapshot.
